subject: Urgent: Checkoutly p95 latency surge investigation & mitigation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] Checkoutly - p95 latency spike (9:10-9:40 PDT)

Heads up — automated monitoring flagged a sustained p95 spike for Checkoutly between 09:10 and 09:40 PDT (~30m). Symptoms: elevated tokenization and KV cache miss rates, per-request CPU on host group nrt-gpu-pool-7 increased ~2.8x. Attached are a condensed trace and a KV eviction timeline for that window.

What we see so far:
- p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.6s; p99 to ~3.2s.
- autoscaler churned 6 instances (scale down then up) during the window; we see correlated KV cache damage.
- Checkoutly is on Dedicated, heavy embedding+chat mix, traffic surge aligned with their batch job at ~09:05.

Immediate ask: SRE to confirm mitigation path (cache warmup / prefetch / routing) and short customer message. Looping in Product for prioritization if roadmap changes needed.

Attachments: p95-trace-20280422.json, kv-eviction-graph-20280422.png

--
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Checkoutly - p95 latency spike (9:10-9:40 PDT)

Thanks Ben — appreciate the quick capture. Kim, can you confirm whether Checkoutly reported user impact? Nina (Checkoutly VP Eng) is on the thread in the external conversation; we need a concise customer note.

Internal asks:
- Karthik: quick RCA please and list of mitigations we can safely toggle without infra-side deploys. We need an action matrix: immediate mitigation (<=1h), short-term (<=24h), roadmap asks (1-4w).
- Marissa: assess product tradeoffs (quantization vs cache-warmup priority) and whether we should push a focused delivery.
- Ben/Kim: draft an external note for Checkoutly acknowledging the spike, impact, and a near-term fix ETA. Keep it transparent but avoid speculative root cause.

I'll consolidate and propose a customer-facing message after we have the mitigations and ETA.

Vanessa
Account Lead — Dedicated Accounts
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Checkoutly - p95 latency spike (9:10-9:40 PDT)

Quick RCA (initial):
- Root trigger: aggressive scale-down during a short traffic lull coinciding with a scheduled batch that restarted and produced a fanout of requests. Scale-down evicted local KV caches; subsequent cold starts led to high fetch latencies and CPU amplification while models warmed up.
- Amplifiers: Checkoutly's model variant is a larger embed+gen combo (v2-large) with higher KV working set. No per-tenant pre-warm in place.

Immediate mitigations (<=1h):
1) Pin pool for Checkoutly (prevent scale-down) — can be done via routing rule change; low risk, immediate effect.
2) Enable short-term request-level KV warmup on hot paths (best-effort prefetch hook) — needs a runtime toggle; Ben, can you flip?

Short-term (<=24h):
- Configure per-tenant warmup hooks + protective rate limit for batch jobs.
- Adjust autoscaler policy for smaller teardown windows for dedicated pools serving large models.

Product/roadmap asks (1-4w):
- Expose per-tenant cache pre-warm controls in Dedicated console (Marissa).
- Add a low-cost model variant (v2-medium) to the model catalog for fallback routing during warmup.
- Investigate smarter autoscaler heuristics that consider KV occupancy.

Risks: Pinning reduces multi-tenant efficiency; warmup hooks add minor cost. Overall recommended order: pin pool now, warmup toggle now, config changes in 24h, UI/variant work as roadmap items.

I can action the first two if Ben gives the runtime thumbs-up.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer

> Attachment: proposed-mitigation-checklist.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Checkoutly - p95 latency spike (9:10-9:40 PDT)

Thanks — this aligns with product expectations. Prioritization notes from my side:
- Console pre-warm control (self-serve) is high value for Dedicated customers with predictable batch windows; we should scope a simple toggle + API first (2 sprints).
- v2-medium fallback: viable but requires validation on quality regressions for Checkoutly's prompt sets; propose a canary route for new requests while preserving strict affinity for in-flight sessions.

Roadmap ask: can Engineering provide a recommendation (cost delta and dev effort) for:
A) Implementing per-tenant warmup toggle exposed via API (low effort, immediate value).
B) Building fallback routing to v2-medium with automated quality gating (medium effort, 3-4 weeks).

Customer comms: we should offer Checkoutly the pinned pool + warmup toggle now and a follow-up roadmap note that a console toggle and fallback variant work is scheduled. Kim, please propose language that offers a credit or SLA gesture if impact was user-facing.

Marissa
Director, Product — Serving
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina@checkoutly.com>, checkoutly-support@checkoutly.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Checkoutly: brief on this morning's p95 latency spike and immediate next steps

Nina —

Thanks for raising this with us and apologies for the disruption this morning. We saw a p95 latency increase impacting a subset of Checkoutly workloads between ~09:10–09:40 PDT. Our initial investigation found the spike was caused by cache evictions during automated scale activity coinciding with a scheduled Checkoutly batch job. The result was higher-than-normal model warmup time on a portion of requests.

What we did immediately:
- Prevented additional scale-down events for your Dedicated pool (pins applied).
- Enabled a runtime warmup prefetch on hot request paths to reduce cold starts.

What we will do next:
- Configure per-tenant warmup controls and protective rate-limits within 24 hours.
- Evaluate adding a validated lower-cost model variant as a fallback route; we will share a timeline within 2–3 weeks.

Customer impact: we observed elevated p95 for a 30-minute window; we are happy to review logs with your engineering team and quantify any user-facing effects. If you saw measurable customer impact, Kimberly will coordinate a credit/SLA conversation.

If you'd like a short sync with our SRE and Product leads, we're available today afternoon.

Thanks for your patience — we'll follow up with a post-incident note once we finish a deeper RCA.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead — Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference
